def f(x, lst=[]):
    lst.append(x)
    return lst

print(f(1))
print(f(2))

What does this print?
explanation: Default argument values are evaluated ONCE, when the function is defined - not on every call. Since lst=[] creates one list object at definition time, every call that omits lst shares and mutates that SAME list, so it accumulates across calls instead of resetting.
